sections.title: Definisi dan Prinsip Rehabilitasi

content.text: Rehabilitation is a dynamic process to help a person achieve optimal physical, emotional, psychological, social, and vocational potential while maintaining dignity and self-respect. Neurorehabilitation specifically aims to aid recovery from nervous system injury and minimize or compensate for functional alterations. Rehabilitation should begin at initial patient contact.

GOALS: Restore patient to independence or regain pre-illness status; maximize independence within disability limits; realize goals based on individual assessment; active patient participation; facilitate activities of daily living (ADL); motivate patient toward social independence.

TYPES: Medical rehabilitation (restoration of structure and function); Vocational rehabilitation (restoration of earning capacity); Social rehabilitation (restoration of family and social relationships); Psychological rehabilitation (restoration of personal dignity and confidence). APPROACHES: Institution-based, outreach-based, community-based (Rehabilitasi Berbasis Masyarakat).

sections.title: Tim Rehabilitasi Neuro

content.text: The neurorehabilitation team is multidisciplinary. Physicians include physiatrist, orthopedic surgeon, neurologist, neurosurgeon, psychiatrist, and pediatrician. Paramedical members include physiotherapist, occupational therapist, speech pathologist, rehabilitation nurse, psychologist, social worker, and vocational counselor.

sections.title: Positioning dan Transfer

content.text: POSITIONING prevents musculoskeletal deformities, contractures, ankylosis, pressure ulcers, decreased vascular supply, thrombosis, and edema. The unconscious patient should be repositioned every 2 hours. Spastic patients require frequent repositioning. Use pillows for body alignment, trochanter rolls, and positioning devices. For weak or paralyzed arms, position to approximate glenoid cavity; use axillary pillow to prevent adduction. For feet, use high-top sneakers or splints to prevent foot drop and pressure ulcers.

TRANSFER TYPES: Two-person lift (no active patient participation); Mechanical lift (lifting device); Contact guard (verbal cues + minimal physical support); Supervision (verbal cues only). Key principles: transfer toward unaffected side; properly fitted flat shoes; never pull on paretic arm; stand on affected side if balance is unsteady; use knee-to-knee block if knees buckle.

HEMIPLEGIC BED-TO-SIT TRANSFER: Move to side of bed; slip unaffected leg under affected leg as transfer cradle; place affected arm on abdomen; push off mattress with unaffected elbow while turning hips; swing unaffected leg over bed edge; push up with unaffected hand; lean on unaffected hand to maintain erect position.

Transfer ke sisi tak terkena
Jangan menarik lengan paretil
Walker atau four-point cane untuk support
Never pull on the paretic arm during transfers - this causes shoulder subluxation and pain

sections.title: Fisioterapi Modalitas

content.text: HEAT THERAPY: Increases blood flow and connective tissue extensibility; decreases joint stiffness, pain, and muscle spasm; reduces inflammation. Types: hot pack, infrared ray, paraffin bath (49 degrees C), hydrotherapy (warm water), diathermy. INDICATIONS: sprains, myositis, arthralgia, neuralgia, muscle spasm, strains. COLD THERAPY: Reduces inflammation, edema, and exudates. ELECTRICAL STIMULATION: For denervated or involuntarily innervated muscle to prevent disuse atrophy and spasticity. TENS (Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation) for chronic low back pain, neuralgia, contusion. TRACTION: For extrinsic muscle spasm, HNP, cervical/lumbar traction. MASSAGE and BIOFEEDBACK (EMG, galvanic skin response).
Heat: hot pack, infrared, paraffin bath 49C, hydrotherapy, diathermy
Cold: reduce inflammation and edema
TENS: chronic low back pain, neuralgia, contusion
Traction: cervical, lumbar for HNP

sections.title: Bobath NDT dan Disfagia

content.text: BOBATH/NDT APPROACH: Used for hemiplegia from stroke, brain injury, and cerebral palsy. Major goal is normalization of muscle tone, posture, movement, and function. Reintegration of both body sides. Proximal-to-distal positioning, weight bearing on affected side, symmetric midline starting position, movement toward affected side encouraged. Straighten trunk and neck to promote symmetry and normalize tone. Position hemiplegic patients opposite to spastic patterns: avoid flexion/adduction in upper extremity and extension in lower extremity.

DYSPHAGIA ASSESSMENT (Simple bedside test): Position patient upright; give 1 teaspoon (5ml) cold water with head slightly flexed; check lip closure during swallow; palpate larynx for elevation; monitor for delayed or incomplete swallow; have patient vocalize 'aaaa' - monitor for wet/hoarse voice; have patient cough and repeat vocalization. If patient cannot swallow or voice becomes wet -> NGT insertion required. Feeding position: upright 90 degrees, head flexed forward, chin tucked, small bites, thorough chewing.
Bobath: normalisasi tonus otot, postur, gerak, fungsi
Disfagia: beri 1 sdt air dingin, palpasi elevasi laring, suara 'aaaa'
Posisi makan: tegak 90 derajat, dagu tuck, suapan kecil
Wet voice after swallowing indicates aspiration - NGT may be needed

sections.title: Manajemen Bladder dan Bowel

content.text: BLADDER MANAGEMENT: Four categories of urinary incontinence: urge (abrupt strong desire to void), stress (loss with coughing/sneezing), overflow (overdistension), functional (factors outside lower urinary tract). Bladder training: education, scheduled voiding (initial interval 2-3 hours), positive reinforcement. Prompted voiding for cognitively impaired: regular monitoring, prompting to use bathroom, praising continence. Pelvic muscle (Kegel) exercises: contract to count of 10, relax to count of 10, 50-100 daily, improvement in 4-6 weeks. Bladder-triggering techniques: suprapubic stimulation, Valsalva maneuver, Crede maneuver.

BOWEL MANAGEMENT: Constipation causes: fluid restriction, immobility, decreased bulk, constipating drugs (codeine), spinal compression, paralytic ileus. Bowel training: ensure lower bowel empty (enema if needed), establish regular timing based on previous pattern, high roughage diet, increase fluid to 2000-2500 mL/day, suppository on first day, seated position for defecation.
Bladder training: scheduled voiding tiap 2-3 jam
Kegel: kontraksi 10 detik, relaksasi 10 detik, 50-100x/hari

sections.title: Rehabilitasi Spesifik

content.text: STROKE REHABILITATION: Goals - optimize recovery, modify residual symptoms, achieve independent functional activity, environmental adaptation, quality of life. Three phases: Acute (first 2 weeks, hemodynamic stabilization, prevent complications); Subacute (2 weeks-6 months, restore ADL, walking, life roles); Chronic (>6 months, endurance and muscle strengthening). Principles: maximize movement, functional movement goals, sitting and standing stability, 45-60 minute sessions, cognitive function support. Complications of prolonged bed rest: cardiovascular (DVT risk, orthostatic hypotension), respiratory (retention, pneumonia), musculoskeletal (weakness, contracture, osteoporosis), metabolic (decreased glucose tolerance), integumentary (pressure ulcers), GI (constipation), GU (urinary incontinence), CNS (decreased cognition).

BRAIN INJURY: Positioning, supportive eating and standing, motor control rehabilitation, bowel/bladder care, pain management, balance training, memory aids. SPINAL CORD INJURY: Safe transportation, traction, positioning, active/passive ROM, mat work, orthoses, gait training, mobility training. PARKINSONISM: Reduce rigidity and maintain flexibility, balance training, coordination exercises, breathing and chest expansion exercises.
